chapter: Learning from players; Jonah Jones lessons
title: Walter Fuller, Don Redman, Andy Kirk and Shorty Baker mix-ups
summary: Maxwell mixes up Don Redman's job and Mary Lou Williams's husband; Hinton corrects him.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Another trumpet player I used to like was Walter Fuller in Earl Hines' band. I used to listen to him a lot. See, out in California I didn't have too much choice of who I could hear. There was a good trumpet player, Don Redman had a good trumpet -- I think it was Red Allen, made a tune called "Shaking the African". And it starts off with this wild solo (humming). And then Don Redman sings. God, he was -- what a giant he was. And he wound up in the union being a sergeant at arms or something, dumb thing.
Who was that?
Don Redman.
Oh, he was a saxophone player.
No, in recent years he's worked up at 802, until he died.
That's Andy Kirk.
No, Don Redman, too. I know Andy Kirk's up there but --
Are you talking about a trumpet player, short, dark man?
No, I'm talking about Don Redman, used to have a band.
He was an orchestra arranger?
Yeah.
Oh, he wrote until he died.
I thought he was working up at the union.
No, that's --
I know Andy Kirk's up there.
No, there was another man that was in the Delegates for Harlem, trumpet player, but his name was Kenneth Roarc Mr. Roarc Kenneth Roarc.
I'm talking about Don Redman. Somebody told me that and told me wrong.
I'm sure that's wrong.
Okay. Because I was thinking -- well, even Andy Kirk shouldn't be up there as a delegate, he should be on a pension, you know.
Yeah, he's a magnificent man. I just had some good reports tonight, did you tell me or somebody told me that they asked him to take a 10 piece band to Japan or some place like that.
Oh, really. That will be great. He had a trumpet player I was crazy about, too. Mary Lou William's husband, Shorty Baker.
No, he wasn't Mary Louis' husband?
He wasn't?
HEMLOCK
May I correct you. John Williams was a baritone sax player, was her husband.
I thought Harold Baker was?
No, he might have been a close friend.
Maybe I just came to the wrong conclusion.
(Laughter.)
Hey, you all, don't pay any attention to that. No, Shorty Baker was in that band, a magnificent trumpet player.
Oh, was he ever.
And I can't say that they didn't come to be friends later, but her husband was a baritone saxophone player in the Andy Kirk's band.
